Religious doubt permits honest presentation of competing views, but durable good conduct still depends on God-centered institutions that provide daily cultural reinforcement and social support.

The closing argument answers the honesty objection while restating the pro side's central claim that individual secular encouragement cannot replace the networks and authority of religious institutions.
O'Connor's argument that unbelievers cannot manufacture sincere faith or responsibly transmit beliefs they regard as false for the sake of social utility.
